avoid_supplements.name: High-dose phosphate binders (calcium carbonate, sevelamer)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Tenapanor increases intestinal phosphate excretion; concurrent phosphate binders may cause hypophosphatemia and reduce tenapanor efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Coordinate phosphate management with prescriber; space dosing if binders necessary

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose calcium supplements (>1000 mg/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May bind tenapanor in GI tract and reduce absorption; can also interfere with phosphate balance
avoid_supplements.action: Use lower doses or obtain from food sources; separate administration by 2+ hours if needed

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Tenapanor's effects on intestinal ion transport may alter iron absorption dynamics
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of iron deficiency; consider iron status labs periodically

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: NHE3 inhibition may affect overall divalent cation absorption; monitor serum levels
caution_supplements.action: Assess magnesium status at baseline and during therapy if supplementing

caution_foods.name: High phosphate foods (processed meats, dairy, nuts, seeds)
caution_foods.mechanism: Tenapanor increases phosphate excretion; excessive dietary phosphate may counteract therapeutic benefit in hyperphosphatemia
caution_foods.action: Patient education on moderate phosphate intake; coordinate with renal dietitian if applicable

caution_foods.name: Foods high in sodium
caution_foods.mechanism: Tenapanor reduces intestinal sodium reabsorption; high sodium diet may partially offset mechanism
caution_foods.action: Counsel on sodium restriction consistent with clinical indication

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum phosphate, electrolytes (sodium, magnesium, calcium), and renal function periodically. Assess GI tolerance as tenapanor commonly causes diarrhea, which may be exacerbated by certain supplements or dietary patterns.
